newsitem.title: USA: FDA committee backs new treatment for diabetes.
newsitem.headline: FDA committee backs new treatment for diabetes.

text.p: Federal health authorities on Wednesday took a first step toward approving a new drug to treat an increasingly prevalent type of diabetes that cannot be controlled with insulin.

An advisory committee to the Food and Drug Administration recommended unanimously that the FDA approve the Warner-Lambert Co. drug Rezulin to treat Type two diabetes, which affects about three million Americans.
Its recommendation is not binding on the FDA, but the agency usually accepts the views of its advisory committees.
Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory panel members said they had little doubt Rezulin was effective and that the minor risks it posed were far outweighed by its benefits.

Type two diabetes is a metabolic disorder resulting from the body's inability to make enough insulin, or to properly use it, to convert sugar, starches and other foods into the energy required for daily life.
This condition is treated by insulin injection therapy.
Warner-Lambert officials said Rezulin, taken as a tablet once a day, was found effective in trials as a therapy for patients whose diabetes does not respond to insulin.
Medical experts say the cause of diabetes is a mystery, although genetics and factors such as obesity and a lack of exercise appear to play roles.
They add that Type two is nearing epidemic stage, due to an increased number of older Americans and a greater prevalence of obesity and a sedentary lifestyle.
Type one diabetes is an autoimmune disease in which the body produces no insulin and most often occurs in younger people.
All told, about 7.6 million people in the United States have diabetes. It is the fourth leading cause of death and this year some 178,000 Americans will die of it, experts say.

Rezulin was discovered by Sankyo Co. Ltd. of Japan, where it has been approved for marketing, and is being developed for the U.S. market by Warner-Lambert's Parke Davis Pharmaceutical Research division.
Warner-Lambert said it intended to ask the FDA early next year to approve Rezulin to treat other types of diabetes as well as the Type two.
